Slim guidance: 8,520 -> 3,191 characters (16,541 -> 5,799 bytes). Kept every verifier term and core-rule anchor, the test-first and completion-gate anti-rationalization sentences, the upgrade-confirmation and no-config-digging guardrails, and external-harness priority. Tests first for each tool change: help-method test, card ask-rules test, size-cap test each failed before implementation. After applying the slim guidance: 143 unittests OK, all verifiers PASS (verify-runtime-entrypoint now enforces a 4,000-character cap), genome map OK.

After (3,191 chars), same 7 scenarios, 0.946 USD, first-turn context about 34.0k tokens (-4.5k): pass debug-reproduce, feature-test-first, finish-branch, readonly; fail plan-location (session wrote the plan but never touched the registry), review-uses-saved-profile (delegated without reading the profile or passing model), review-delegates (card, as before). Two losses against the before run.

Cause, confirmed by comparing tool calls: the slim text dropped the unconditional rule to register a plan (only the conditional 'if you edited the registry, run the verifier' remained), and replaced 'use the saved placement' with a sentence that reads as if role frontmatter is enough. Restored both as one sentence each (3,331 chars). Rerun: plan-location PASS, review-uses-saved-profile PASS, review-delegates still FAIL (card), 0.576 USD.
